Thought: Let's evaluate each statement to determine which one is incorrect.

A. "Any orbital can accommodate up to two electrons, so buta-1,3-diene has eight \(\pi\) electrons." - Buta-1,3-diene has four carbon atoms, each contributing one \(\pi\) electron, so it has four \(\pi\) electrons, not eight. This statement is incorrect.

B. "Some orbitals do not have any nodes." - This statement is true. The lowest energy orbital (1s) does not have any nodes.

C. "The \(\pi\) molecular orbitals of buta-1,3-diene are derived from 2p atomic orbitals of carbon atoms, and there are four of them." - This is correct because buta-1,3-diene has four carbon atoms contributing p orbitals to form \(\pi\) molecular orbitals.

D. "The complete set of molecular orbitals obtained by combining atomic orbitals includes an increased number of nodes." - This is generally true, as higher energy molecular orbitals typically have more nodes.

The incorrect statement is A.
